result.text: We characterized the melting of a bulk Ni sample using molecular dynamics with LAMMPS. The initial condition was obtained by replicating the Ni unit cell 10 times in each direction. Initial velocities were drawn from the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at 600 K. The system was heated from 300 K to 2500 K continuously, at a rate of 10 K per ps under isothermal and isobaric conditions at 1 atm. Interactions were described using an embedded atom model developed by Mishin et al. in 1999 [1] obtained from OpenKIM.org. [1] EAM potential (LAMMPS cubic hermite tabulation) for Ni developed by Mishin et al. (1999) v005. OpenKIM; 2018. doi:10.25950/a88dfc37.

result.sanitized_script:
units metal
atom_style atomic
boundary p p p
lattice fcc 3.52
region box block 0 1 0 1 0 1
create_box 1 box
create_atoms 1 box
replicate 10 10 10
mass 1 58.6934
pair_style eam/alloy
pair_coeff * * Ni_Mishin_1999.eam.alloy Ni
velocity all create 600 482793 mom yes rot yes dist gaussian
timestep 0.001
fix 1 all npt temp 300 2500 0.1 iso 1 1 1
thermo 1000
thermo_style custom step time temp press vol pe ke etotal density
run 220000

result.text:
Domain review against the method description:

[NOTE] Initial-velocity temperature mismatch is intrinsic to the prompt: velocities are seeded at 600 K while the NPT thermostat is ramped from 300 K to 2500 K. The script reproduces this exactly. The thermostat will rapidly damp the kinetic temperature toward 300 K within a few T-damp times (0.1 ps), so the practical effect is small, but the discrepancy was carried through verbatim from the description.

[NOTE] Units and quantities are consistent with metal units: lattice parameter 3.52 A (FCC Ni), mass 58.6934 g/mol, pressure 1.0 bar (1 atm = 1.01325 bar; 0.3% off, acceptable), timestep 0.001 ps = 1 fs.

[NOTE] Heating schedule: 300 K -> 2500 K at 10 K/ps gives 220 ps total. With dt = 0.001 ps that is exactly 220,000 steps, matching the 'run 220000' line.

[NOTE] Geometry: lattice fcc with region 0-1 + replicate 10 10 10 yields 10x10x10 conventional FCC cells = 4000 atoms (4 atoms/cell), matching 'replicating the Ni unit cell 10 times in each direction'. Periodic boundaries on all faces are correct for a bulk sample.

[NOTE] Potential: the Mishin 1999 Ni EAM file shipped as prompt2.potential is in setfl format ('1 Ni' header line), so pair_style eam/alloy with one element label 'Ni' is correct. The OpenKIM 'cubic hermite tabulation' refers to the same setfl-format file used here.

[NOTE] NPT damping constants (Tdamp = 0.1 ps, Pdamp = 1.0 ps) are physically reasonable for metal units.

No physical correctness warnings. The script faithfully reproduces the described protocol.
